topics.label: Introduction to cancer hallmarks and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: These remarks introduce the lecture objectives and outline the framework of cancer hallmarks.

topics.label: Growth signal autonomy and oncogenic signaling cascades
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations in cell surface receptors and intracellular cascades drive sustained proliferative signaling.

topics.label: Block to terminal cell differentiation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how cancer cells fail to execute terminal differentiation in haematopoietic and epithelial tissues.

topics.label: Evasion of apoptosis and regulation of cell death
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores how alterations in p53 and Bcl-2 family proteins prevent programmed cell death in cancer cells.

topics.label: Replicative immortality, senescence, and stress responses
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address telomere maintenance, senescence bypass mechanisms, and p53-mediated responses to cellular stress before concluding the growth-control hallmarks.

topics.label: Cancer metabolism and metabolic rewiring
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the mechanisms and consequences of altered cellular metabolism, aerobic glycolysis, and oncometabolite production in tumors.

topics.label: Tumor angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes the necessity, timing, and molecular regulation of new blood vessel formation to sustain tumor growth.

topics.label: Tumor invasion, dissemination, and metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover the multistep process of cancer metastasis, including systemic dissemination, liquid biopsies, colonization efficiency, and genomic profiles.

topics.label: Conclusion and final summary
topics.groupedBecause: These closing remarks summarise the key themes of the lecture and provide concluding guidance.
